proposal: When ingesting ANY multi-source or multi-voice content into a retrieval store (conversations, interviews, multi-author docs, agent-bus transcripts), always carry source/speaker provenance INSIDE each chunk — a per-unit label (prefix every paragraph with its speaker) AND a chunk-level frame ("[conversation with X, DATE]"). Rationale: retrieval returns chunks out of context, and chunk-boundary splitting silently drops attribution present in the source; unlabeled multi-voice content risks the reader adopting others' words as its own (basement L13, instance 7). Monologue sources (single-author essays, logs) don't need this; dialogue/multi-source does. Concretely: never chunk a joined transcript blindly — ensure chunk boundaries fall on speaker-labeled units. L13's prevention recipe as a standing ingest practice.
